en.B: A song. A psalm of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song, a psalm: two words for a song
decisions.reason: Song (shir) is the general word; psalm (mizmor) is a song sung to music (48:1).

decisions.choice: a psalm made of two others
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 joins the end of Psalm 57 (57:8-12 = 108:2-6) to the end of Psalm 60 (60:7-14 = 108:7-14), with a few small changes. The new song leaves out the trouble that opened both psalms and keeps their praise and their prayer for victory.

decisions.choice: a song with music
decisions.reason: As in 48:1, Readable joins the two words into one plain phrase.

decisions.choice: shir is "un cantique" (Literal, Balanced) and mizmor "un psaume"; Readable says "un chant", for the psalm titles of Psalms 105–118
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words both name a sung poem (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep two French words, as the English keeps "song" and "psalm"; Readable says what the title means in one plain phrase, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Cántico. Salmo (L, B); Canto con música (R)
decisions.reason: The title joins shir (a song) and mizmor (a song sung to music). As in the other psalm titles, Literal and Balanced say "Cántico" and "Salmo" without the article; Readable joins them in "Canto con música", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "bài ca" for shir and "thi thiên" for mizmor (L, B), as Psalm 30:1; Readable joins them as "Bài ca có nhạc đệm"
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words are kept apart as in the earlier Psalms; Readable says what the pair means, as the English Readable's "a song with music". |

decisions.choice: "노래" for shir and "시" for mizmor (L, B); Readable "다윗이 지은 ... 노래", with "악기에 맞춰" for mizmor
decisions.reason: As the terms note and style guide section 7a: a psalm's title is translated at every level, Literal and Balanced keeping the Hebrew's two words, Readable saying what they mean, a song David made, sung to music (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Cântico. Salmo de Davi. (L, B); Uma canção com música (R); verses 2-14 in the words of Psalms 57 and 60
alternatives: a new wording for the joined psalm
decisions.reason: The title has the words of 48:1 and 83:1 in Portuguese. Since the psalm joins 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m3), its Portuguese repeats theirs at each level wherever the Hebrew is the same, and changes only where this psalm's Hebrew does: one "o meu coração está firme" and "a minha glória" with the singing (2), the name SENHOR for "meu Senhor" (4), "acima dos céus" (5) and the last line of verse 10.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of Psalm 108
decisions.reason: Amharic has no deity_pronoun spans: the Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. God is spoken of with the ordinary pronouns (እርሱ, አንተ) at every level.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 keeps the Amharic of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 wherever the Hebrew is the same
decisions.reason: The psalm is made of the ends of Psalms 57 and 60 (see the meaning decision). Where the Hebrew differs (verses 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 and 12) the Amharic follows this psalm's Hebrew, and a decision on the verse says so.

decisions.choice: गीत, भजन as in 48:1
decisions.reason: The title pairs shir and mizmor; Hindi gives them as in Psalm 48:1, with "A psalm of David" as "दाऊद का भजन" as in Psalms 3-41; Readable joins them into one plain phrase as the English does, with "दाऊद का लिखा हुआ" for "by David", as in Psalms 24 and 25.

decisions.choice: Песнь. Псалом (L, B); Песня с музыкой (R)
decisions.reason: The poetry note's words for shir and mizmor; the psalm joins Psalm 57:8-12 and 60:7-14, and each level copies their Russian wherever the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: shir mizmor "歌。…賛歌。" (L, B), "音楽に合わせた歌" (R); ledavid with mizmor "ダビデの賛歌" (L, B), "ダビデによる" (R)
decisions.reason: The Psalter's title forms (PSA-1; 83:1, 87:1 R for the English R 'a song with music'). The title is verse 1 (m1), prose at every level.

decisions.choice: Verses 2–14 keep the Ukrainian wording of 57:8–12 and 60:7–14 wherever the sense is the same, and differ only where this psalm differs
decisions.reason: Readers comparing the psalms should see the same words where the source repeats itself and a change only where it changes.

source.text: נָכ֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אָשִׁ֥ירָה וַ֝אֲזַמְּרָ֗ה אַף־כְּבוֹדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Steadfast [is] my heart, God; I will sing and I will make music, also my glory.

en.L: Steadfast [is] my heart, God; I will sing and make music, even [with] my glory.
en.B: My heart is firm, God; I will sing and play songs of praise with all my soul.
en.R: God, my heart is calm and sure. I am ready to sing and to play music in praise of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all that I am.

fr.L: Ferme [est] mon cœur, ô Dieu ; je chanterai et je jouerai, et même [avec] ma gloire.
fr.B: Mon cœur est ferme, ô Dieu ; je chanterai et je jouerai des chants de louange de toute mon âme.
fr.R: Mon Dieu, mon cœur est calme et confiant. Je suis prêt à chanter et à jouer de la musique pour {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louer de tout mon être.

sw.L: Moyo wangu [ni] thabiti, Ee Mungu; nitaimba na kupiga muziki, hata [kwa] utukufu wangu.
sw.B: Moyo wangu u imara, Ee Mungu; nitaimba na kupiga nyimbo za sifa kwa nafsi yangu yote.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, moyo wangu umetulia na una uhakika. Niko tayari kuimba na kupiga muziki kukusifu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} kwa utu wangu wote.

es.L: Firme [está] mi corazón, oh Dios; cantaré y tocaré música, también [con] mi gloria.
es.B: Mi corazón está firme, oh Dios; cantaré y tocaré cantos de alabanza con toda el alma.
es.R: Dios, mi corazón está tranquilo y seguro. Estoy listo para cantar y tocar música para alabarte con todo mi ser.

vi.L: Lòng tôi vững vàng, lạy Đức Chúa Trời; tôi sẽ hát và đàn ca, cả [với] vinh quang của tôi.
vi.B: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, lòng tôi vững vàng; tôi sẽ hết lòng hát và gảy đàn ca ngợi.
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, lòng tôi bình tĩnh và vững chắc. Tôi sẵn sàng hát và chơi nhạc ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} với cả con người tôi.

ko.L: 하나님, 제 마음이 확고합니다. 제가 노래하고 찬송을 연주하겠습니다. 제 영광으로도 [그리하겠습니다].
ko.B: 하나님, 제 마음이 굳건합니다. 제가 온 마음을 다해 노래하며 찬송을 연주하겠습니다.
ko.R: 하나님, 제 마음은 평안하고 든든합니다. 저는 온 힘을 다해 노래하고 악기를 연주하며 주님을 찬양할 준비가 되어 있습니다.

pt.L: O meu coração [está] firme, ó Deus; cantarei e farei música, também [com] a minha glória.
pt.B: O meu coração está firme, ó Deus; vou cantar e tocar louvores com toda a minha alma.
pt.R: Ó Deus, o meu coração está tranquilo e seguro. Estou pronto para cantar e tocar música em louvor a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} com tudo o que eu sou.

am.L: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ልቤ ጽኑ ነው፤ እቀኛለሁ፤ እዘምራለሁም፤ ክብሬም ጭምር [ይዘምራል]።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ልቤ ጸንቷል፤ በሙሉ ነፍሴ እዘምራለሁ፤ የምስጋና ዜማም እጫወታለሁ።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ልቤ የተረጋጋና የጸና ነው። አንተን ለማመስገን በሙሉ ማንነቴ ልዘምርና በመሣሪያ ልጫወት ተዘጋጅቻለሁ።

hi.L: मेरा हृदय दृढ़ [है], हे परमेश्वर; मैं गाऊँगा और बाजा बजाकर स्तुति करूँगा, अपनी महिमा [से] भी।
hi.B: हे परमेश्वर, मेरा हृदय स्थिर है; मैं पूरे मन से गाऊँगा और बाजे पर स्तुति के गीत बजाऊँगा।
hi.R: हे परमेश्वर, मेरा मन शांत और निश्चिंत है। मैं अपने पूरे मन से तेरी स्तुति में गाने और बाजा बजाने को तैयार हूँ।

ru.L: Твёрдо моё сердце, Боже; я буду петь и играть, и [с] моей славой.
ru.B: Моё сердце непоколебимо, Боже; я буду петь и играть хвалебные песни всей душой.
ru.R: Боже, моё сердце спокойно и уверенно. Я готов петь и играть музыку во славу {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} всем своим существом.

ja.L: わたしの心は揺るがない、神よ。わたしは歌い、ほめ歌を歌おう、わたしの栄光も[共に]。
ja.B: 神よ、わたしの心は定まった。わたしは歌い、わたしの魂をこめて、ほめ歌を奏でよう。
ja.R: 神よ、わたしの心は落ち着いて、しっかりしている。わたしは、わたしのすべてをもって、あなたを賛美して歌い、楽器を鳴らそう。

uk.L: Тверде моє серце, Боже; я співатиму й гратиму, навіть [усією] моєю славою.
uk.B: Моє серце непохитне, Боже; я співатиму й гратиму пісні хвали всією душею.
uk.R: Боже, моє серце спокійне й упевнене. Я готовий співати й грати музику на хвалу {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} всім своїм єством.

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:8-9
decisions.reason: Verses 2-3 repeat 57:8-9 with two changes: "steadfast is my heart" is said once, not twice, and "my glory" ends this line instead of opening the next ("Wake up, my glory!"). The wording follows 57:8-9.

decisions.choice: steadfast: firm, settled, ready
decisions.reason: As in 57:8 (nakhon): a heart firmly fixed on God (112:7).

decisions.choice: my glory: my inner self
alternatives: my liver (with other vowels), the seat of feeling
decisions.reason: As in 57:9: "my glory" (kavod) is the whole inner being (16:9; 30:13). Here it goes with the singing: he will sing with all he is.

decisions.choice: with all my soul (B); with all that I am (R)
decisions.reason: As in 57:9, Balanced gives the sense of the word; Readable says it plainly (m3).

decisions.choice: in praise of you
decisions.reason: As in 57:8, Readable says whom the music is for.

decisions.choice: con toda el alma (B); con todo mi ser (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "my glory" here is the singer's inner self, his whole being. Literal keeps "mi gloria"; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời" when the singer calls on God; he says "tôi" and speaks to God as "Ngài"
decisions.reason: As in the earlier Psalms, "Lạy" is the word of address prayer requires, unbracketed at Literal. |

decisions.choice: The singer speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저/제" and addresses him as "주님"
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7a (speech levels in prayer); there are no deity_pronoun spans in Korean. The plain style returns where the psalm speaks to the instruments (verse 3), reports God's words (verses 8-10) or speaks about God (verses 11, 14).

decisions.choice: "제 영광" (my glory) kept at Literal; "온 마음을 다해" (B), "온 힘을 다해" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable give its sense here, the whole inner self singing (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "ክብሬም ጭምር [ይዘምራል]" (L), "በሙሉ ነፍሴ" (B), "በሙሉ ማንነቴ" (R) for "even my glory" at the end of the line
decisions.reason: 57:8 says "steadfast is my heart" twice and opens the next line with "Wake up, my glory!"; here the heart line comes once and "my glory" joins the singing. The rest follows the Amharic of 57:8.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi; the psalmist speaks to God with the devotional तू.

decisions.choice: wording of Psalm 57:8-9
decisions.reason: Verses 2-6 are Psalm 57:8-12, and Hindi keeps that psalm's wording at each level. Here the Hebrew says "my heart is steadfast" once, not twice, and brings "my glory" into this verse, so Hindi does the same: अपनी महिमा [से] भी (L), पूरे मन से (B, R).

decisions.choice: и [с] моей славой (L); всей душой (B); всем своим существом (R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 57:8 says "my heart is steadfast" twice and puts "my glory" in the next line; here it is said once and "my glory" closes this line, so the Russian of 57:8 is kept with that change.

decisions.choice: As 57:8 (nakhon "揺るがない" L, "定まった" B, "落ち着いて、しっかりしている" R), without its repeated half-line; 'af-kevodi "わたしの栄光も[共に]" (L), "わたしの魂をこめて" (B), "わたしのすべてをもって" (R)
decisions.reason: 108:2 takes 57:8 without the repetition of 'my heart is steadfast' and draws in kevodi from 57:9, where the Psalter has わたしの栄光 (L), わたしの魂 (B), わたしの心 (R). Here my glory is the inner self (m3, uncertain); R 'with all that I am' as the English R.

records.literal_gloss: Awake, the harp and lyre! I will awaken [the] dawn.

en.L: Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
en.B: Come awake, harp and lyre! I will wake up the dawn.
en.R: Harp and lyre, wake up! I will be up singing before the sun rises.

fr.L: Réveillez-vous, harpe et lyre ! J’éveillerai l’aurore.
fr.B: Éveillez-vous, harpe et lyre ! Je réveillerai l’aurore.
fr.R: Harpe et lyre, réveillez-vous ! Je serai debout à chanter avant le lever du soleil.

sw.L: Amkeni, zeze na kinubi! Nitaiamsha alfajiri.
sw.B: Amkeni sasa, zeze na kinubi! Nitaiamsha alfajiri.
sw.R: Zeze na kinubi, amkeni! Nitaamka niimbe kabla jua halijachomoza.

es.L: ¡Despierten, arpa y lira! Despertaré a la aurora.
es.B: ¡Arpa y lira, despierten! Yo despertaré al alba.
es.R: ¡Arpa y lira, despierten! Me levantaré a cantar antes de que salga el sol.

vi.L: Hãy thức dậy, đàn hạc và đàn lia! Tôi sẽ đánh thức bình minh.
vi.B: Hãy tỉnh thức, hỡi đàn hạc và đàn lia! Tôi sẽ đánh thức rạng đông.
vi.R: Hỡi đàn hạc và đàn lia, hãy thức dậy! Tôi sẽ dậy hát ca trước khi mặt trời mọc.

ko.L: 하프야, 수금아, 깨어나라! 내가 새벽을 깨우겠다.
ko.B: 하프야, 수금아, 깨어나라! 내가 새벽을 깨우겠다.
ko.R: 하프야, 수금아, 일어나라! 나는 해가 뜨기 전에 일어나 노래하겠다.

pt.L: Despertem, harpa e lira! Eu despertarei a aurora.
pt.B: Acordem, harpa e lira! Vou acordar a aurora.
pt.R: Harpa e lira, acordem! Vou estar de pé cantando antes de o sol nascer.

am.L: በገናና መሰንቆ ሆይ፣ ንቁ! ንጋትን እቀሰቅሳለሁ።
am.B: በገናና መሰንቆ ሆይ፣ ንቁ! ንጋትን እቀሰቅሳለሁ።
am.R: በገናና መሰንቆ፣ ንቁ! ፀሐይ ሳትወጣ ተነሥቼ እዘምራለሁ።

hi.L: जागो, हे सारंगी और वीणा! मैं भोर को जगाऊँगा।
hi.B: हे सारंगी और वीणा, जाग उठो! मैं भोर को जगा दूँगा।
hi.R: हे सारंगी और वीणा, जागो! मैं सूरज निकलने से पहले ही उठकर गाऊँगा।

ru.L: Пробудись, арфа и лира! Я разбужу зарю.
ru.B: Пробудитесь, арфа и лира! Я разбужу зарю.
ru.R: Арфа и лира, проснитесь! Я встану петь ещё до восхода солнца.

ja.L: 目覚めよ、琴よ、竪琴よ！わたしは暁を呼び覚まそう。
ja.B: 目を覚ませ、琴よ、竪琴よ！わたしは夜明けを呼び覚まそう。
ja.R: 琴よ、たて琴よ、目を覚ませ！わたしは、日がのぼる前から起きて歌おう。

uk.L: Прокиньтеся, арфо й ліро! Я розбуджу світанок.
uk.B: Прокиньтеся, арфо й ліро! Я розбуджу зорю.
uk.R: Арфо й ліро, прокиньтеся! Я співатиму ще до сходу сонця.

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:9
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 57:9; the wording here follows it.

decisions.choice: harp and lyre: stringed instruments
decisions.reason: Two stringed instruments used in worship (33:2).

decisions.choice: wake the dawn: be up praising before sunrise
decisions.reason: Instead of the dawn waking him, he will wake the dawn with his song.

decisions.choice: I will be up singing before the sun rises
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).

decisions.choice: "zeze" for the harp (nevel) and "kinubi" for the lyre (kinnor), as Psalm 57:9 and 150:3
decisions.reason: Both Hebrew instruments are plucked strings. Swahili names two kinds, so the reader hears two instruments without a foreign word: "kinubi" for the lyre and "zeze" for the harp, the pairing used through the Psalms, Samuel and Chronicles. The verse keeps the wording of Psalm 57:9.

decisions.choice: Plain style with "나" when the singer calls to his instruments
alternatives: 저 and 합쇼체 as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The singer turns from God to call on the harp and lyre, and Korean speaks to them as one speaks to things, calling oneself "나"; the prayer to God resumes in 합쇼체 in verse 4. "하프" and "수금" name two stringed instruments (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: The Amharic of 57:9 without its first line
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of 108:3 lacks "Wake up, my glory!", which 108:2 has taken up; the rest is word for word 57:9.

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:9 without "Wake up, my glory"
decisions.reason: The wording is that of Psalm 57:9; its first line, the call to "my glory", is not in the Hebrew here (it moved into verse 2).

decisions.choice: As 57:9 without its first line ('uri kevodi): nevel "琴", kinnor "竪琴" (L, B), "たて琴" (R); shachar "暁" (L), "夜明け" (B)
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew as the second and third lines of 57:9 (m1), copied from it; waking the dawn is praising before sunrise (m3).

records.literal_gloss: I will thank you among [the] peoples, YHWH, and I will make music to you among [the] nations.

en.L: I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the peoples, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the nations.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before all peoples; I will sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise in every nation.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in front of people everywhere. I will sing songs of praise to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in every country.

fr.L: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rendrai grâce parmi les peuples, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; je jouerai pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} parmi les nations.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rendrai grâce devant tous les peuples ; je chanterai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} louange dans toutes les nations.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercierai devant les gens du monde entier. Je chanterai des chants de louange pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} dans tous les pays.

sw.L: Nitakushukuru kati ya watu, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; nitakuimbia sifa kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakushukuru mbele ya watu wote; nitaimba sifa {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} katika kila taifa.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakushukuru mbele ya watu kila mahali. Nitakuimbia nyimbo za sifa katika kila nchi.

es.L: Entre los pueblos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alabaré, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; entre las naciones {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré salmos.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré gracias delante de todos los pueblos; cantaré {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} alabanzas en todas las naciones.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré gracias delante de la gente de todas partes. En todos los países {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré alabanzas.

vi.L: Tôi sẽ cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giữa các dân, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; tôi sẽ đàn ca cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giữa các nước.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi sẽ cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trước mọi dân; tôi sẽ hát ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong mọi nước.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi sẽ cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trước mặt mọi người khắp nơi. Tôi sẽ hát những bài ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong mọi quốc gia.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 백성들 가운데서 주님께 감사드리고, 민족들 가운데서 주님께 찬송하겠습니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 모든 백성 앞에서 주님께 감사드리고, 모든 민족 가운데서 주님을 찬양하겠습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 온 세상 사람들 앞에서 주님께 감사드리겠습니다. 모든 나라에서 주님께 찬양의 노래를 부르겠습니다.

pt.L: Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} darei graças entre os povos, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}; cantarei louvores a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} entre as nações.
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} darei graças diante de todos os povos; cantarei o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} louvor em todas as nações.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, vou {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} agradecer diante de gente de todo lugar. Vou cantar louvores a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} em todos os países.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ በወገኖች መካከል አመሰግንሃለሁ፤ በሕዝቦች መካከል እዘምርልሃለሁ።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ በወገኖች ሁሉ ፊት አመሰግንሃለሁ፤ በየአገሩ ሕዝብ መካከል ምስጋናህን እዘምራለሁ።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ በየቦታው ባሉ ሰዎች ፊት አመሰግንሃለሁ። በየአገሩ የምስጋና መዝሙር እዘምርልሃለሁ።

hi.L: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मैं लोगों के बीच तेरा धन्यवाद करूँगा; जातियों के बीच मैं बाजा बजाकर तेरी स्तुति करूँगा।
hi.B: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मैं सब लोगों के सामने तेरा धन्यवाद करूँगा; हर राष्ट्र में मैं तेरी स्तुति के गीत गाऊँगा।
hi.R: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मैं हर जगह के लोगों के सामने तेरा धन्यवाद करूँगा। मैं हर देश में तेरी स्तुति के गीत गाऊँगा।

ru.L: Я буду благодарить {{deity_pronoun:тебя|Тебя}} среди племён, {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}; я буду петь {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} среди народов.
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, я буду благодарить {{deity_pronoun:тебя|Тебя}} перед всеми племенами; я буду воспевать {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} хвалу в каждом народе.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, я буду благодарить {{deity_pronoun:тебя|Тебя}} перед людьми повсюду. Я буду петь {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} хвалебные песни в каждой стране.

ja.L: わたしは、もろもろの民の間であなたに感謝する、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ。民らの間で、あなたにほめ歌を歌う。
ja.B: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ、わたしは、すべての民の前であなたに感謝し、民らの間で、あなたにほめ歌を歌う。
ja.R: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ、わたしは、世界中の人々の前で、あなたに感謝する。どこの国でも、あなたをたたえて歌を歌う。

uk.L: Я дякуватиму {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} серед племен, {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}; я гратиму {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} серед народів.
uk.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, я дякуватиму {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} перед усіма племенами; я співатиму {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} хвалу в кожному народі.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, я дякуватиму {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} перед людьми всюди. Я співатиму пісні хвали {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} в кожній країні.

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:10
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 57:10, but where 57:10 says "my Lord" ('Adonai), this verse has the name YHWH. The wording otherwise follows 57:10.

decisions.choice: among the peoples: praise heard by all nations
decisions.reason: As in 57:10, the psalmist will praise God before the nations, so that they too may know him (18:50; 96:3).

decisions.choice: among the nations: an unusual spelling
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes "among the nations" in an unusual way, so that the first part looks like the word "not". The sense is the same as in 57:10, which has the usual spelling.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ" where 57:10 has "ጌታዬ ሆይ" / "ጌታ ሆይ"
decisions.reason: 57:10 has Adonai; this verse has the name YHWH, so it takes the divine_name span. The rest follows the Amharic of 57:10.

decisions.choice: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}
decisions.reason: Psalm 57:10 has the title Adonai ("my Lord", outside the setting); here the Hebrew has the name YHWH, so the same प्रभु stands inside the divine_name span and the rest of the verse keeps 57:10's wording.

decisions.choice: ГОСПОДИ (the divine_name span)
decisions.reason: Psalm 57:10 has Adonai ("Господь мой", "Господи"); here the Hebrew has the divine name, so only that word changes.

decisions.choice: племена (peoples); народы (nations)
decisions.reason: One rule for the Psalms: where the English Literal or Balanced says "nations", Russian has "народы"; where it says "peoples" ("ammim, le'ummim"), "племена", as Psalm 57:10 has it. Readable follows its English. The tribes of Israel stay "колена".

decisions.choice: As 57:10, with YHWH "DNよ" in place of 57:10's Adonai "主よ"
decisions.reason: 108:4 has the divine name where 57:10 has Adonai (m1); the divine-name span follows the English, the rest is 57:10's Japanese. bal-'ummim, an unusual spelling (m3), is read as 57:10's 'among the nations' (民らの間で).

records.literal_gloss: For great above [the] heavens [is] your loyal love, and to [the] clouds your faithfulness.

en.L: For great above the heavens [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, and to the clouds {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love towers above the heavens, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness rises to the clouds.
en.R: Your faithful love is higher than the sky. Your faithfulness reaches all the way to the clouds.

fr.L: Car grand au-dessus des cieux [est] {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour loyal, et jusqu’aux nuages {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fidélité.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour fidèle s’élève au-dessus des cieux, et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fidélité monte jusqu’aux nuages.
fr.R: Ton amour fidèle est plus haut que le ciel. Ta fidélité va jusqu’aux nuages.

sw.L: Kwa maana upendo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} usiokoma [ni] mkuu juu ya mbingu, na uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mpaka mawinguni.
sw.B: Kwa maana upendo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} usiokoma umeinuka juu kuliko mbingu, na uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} unafika mawinguni.
sw.R: Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} usiokoma uko juu kuliko anga. Uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} unafika mpaka mawinguni.

es.L: Porque grande, por encima de los cielos, [es] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amor leal, y hasta las nubes {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fidelidad.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amor fiel se eleva por encima de los cielos, y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fidelidad llega hasta las nubes.
es.R: Tu amor fiel es más alto que el cielo. Tu fidelidad llega hasta las nubes.

vi.L: Vì lớn hơn các tầng trời [là] tình yêu thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đến tận các tầng mây sự thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vì tình yêu thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cao vượt trên các tầng trời, và sự thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên đến tận mây xanh.
vi.R: Tình thương không hề thay đổi của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cao hơn bầu trời. Sự thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên đến tận các đám mây.

ko.L: 참으로 주님의 한결같은 사랑은 하늘 위로 크고, 주님의 신실하심은 구름에까지 [닿습니다].
ko.B: 주님의 한결같은 사랑은 하늘보다 높이 솟아 있고, 주님의 신실하심은 구름에까지 이릅니다.
ko.R: 주님의 변함없는 사랑은 하늘보다 높습니다. 주님의 신실하심은 구름에까지 닿습니다.

pt.L: Porque grande acima dos céus [é] o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} amor leal, e até as nuvens a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fidelidade.
pt.B: Pois o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} amor leal se eleva acima dos céus, e a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fidelidade sobe até as nuvens.
pt.R: O {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} amor fiel é mais alto que o céu. A {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fidelidade chega até as nuvens.

am.L: ጽኑ ፍቅርህ ከሰማያት በላይ ታላቅ ነውና፤ ታማኝነትህም እስከ ደመናት።
am.B: ጽኑ ፍቅርህ ከሰማይ በላይ ከፍ ብሏልና፤ ታማኝነትህም እስከ ደመናት ይደርሳል።
am.R: ጽኑ ፍቅርህ ከሰማይ ይልቅ ከፍ ያለ ነው። ታማኝነትህ እስከ ደመናት ድረስ ይደርሳል።

hi.L: क्योंकि तेरा अटल प्रेम आकाश से ऊपर महान [है], और तेरी सच्चाई बादलों तक।
hi.B: क्योंकि तेरा अटल प्रेम आकाश से भी ऊँचा उठता है, और तेरी विश्वासयोग्यता बादलों तक पहुँचती है।
hi.R: तेरा अटल प्रेम आकाश से भी ऊँचा है। तेरी विश्वासयोग्यता बादलों तक पहुँचती है।

ru.L: Ведь велика выше небес {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} неизменная любовь, и до облаков {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} верность.
ru.B: Ведь {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} неизменная любовь поднимается выше небес, и {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} верность восходит до облаков.
ru.R: Твоя неизменная любовь выше неба. Твоя верность достигает самых облаков.

ja.L: まことに、あなたの誠実は大きく、天を超えて[及び]、あなたのまことは雲にまで[及ぶ]。
ja.B: あなたの変わらぬいつくしみは、天よりも高くそびえ、あなたのまことは、雲にまで届く。
ja.R: あなたの変わらぬいつくしみは、空よりも高い。あなたの真実は、雲にまで届いている。

uk.L: Бо велика понад небеса {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} незмінна любов, і до хмар — {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} вірність.
uk.B: Бо {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} незмінна любов здіймається понад небеса, і {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} вірність сягає хмар.
uk.R: Твоя вірна любов вища за небо. Твоя вірність сягає аж до хмар.

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:11
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 57:11, but says "above the heavens" where 57:11 says "to the heavens"; the love is greater still. The wording otherwise follows 57:11.

decisions.choice: above the heavens, to the clouds: beyond measure
decisions.reason: As in 36:6 and 57:11, the height of the sky is the measure of God's love (103:11).

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 107:1.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: God's reliability
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) means that God can be relied on to keep his word.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

decisions.choice: "ከሰማያት በላይ" / "ከሰማይ በላይ" (above the heavens) where 57:11 has "እስከ ሰማያት" (to the heavens)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "above" here; Readable already said "higher than the sky" in 57:11 and is kept.

decisions.choice: आकाश से ऊपर (L); आकाश से भी ऊँचा (B)
decisions.reason: Psalm 57:11 says "to the heavens"; here the Hebrew says "above the heavens", so Literal and Balanced change only that phrase. Readable already says "higher than the sky" in 57:11 and stays the same.

decisions.choice: выше небес
decisions.reason: Psalm 57:11 says "to the heavens"; here the Hebrew says "above the heavens", so Literal and Balanced change that phrase.

decisions.choice: me'al-shamayim "天を超えて" (L), "天よりも高く" (B), where 57:11 has 'ad-shamayim "天にまで"
decisions.reason: 108:5 says 'above the heavens' where 57:11 says 'to the heavens' (m1, m2); the rest is 57:11's Japanese. R already said 空よりも高い in 57:11 and is kept.

source.text: ר֣וּמָה עַל־שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Be exalted above [the] heavens, God, and over all the earth your glory.

en.L: Be exalted above the heavens, God; over all the earth [be] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.
en.B: God, be lifted high above the heavens; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory spread over all the earth.
en.R: God, show that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are higher than the heavens! Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory shine over the whole earth!

fr.L: Élève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} au-dessus des cieux, ô Dieu ; sur toute la terre [soit] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire.
fr.B: Ô Dieu, élève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} bien haut au-dessus des cieux ; que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire s’étende sur toute la terre.
fr.R: Mon Dieu, montre que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es plus haut que les cieux ! Que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire brille sur la terre entière !

sw.L: Utukuzwe juu ya mbingu, Ee Mungu; utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} [uwe] juu ya dunia yote.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, uinuliwe juu kuliko mbingu; utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uenee juu ya dunia yote.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, onyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uko juu kuliko mbingu! Utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na uangaze juu ya dunia nzima!

es.L: Sé exaltado por encima de los cielos, oh Dios; sobre toda la tierra [sea] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria.
es.B: Dios, sé enaltecido por encima de los cielos; que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria se extienda sobre toda la tierra.
es.R: ¡Dios, muestra que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} estás por encima de los cielos! ¡Que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria brille sobre toda la tierra!

vi.L: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được tôn cao trên các tầng trời; trên khắp đất [là] vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được tôn cao trên các tầng trời; nguyện vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trải khắp đất.
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, xin tỏ ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cao hơn các tầng trời! Xin cho vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chiếu rạng trên khắp đất!

ko.L: 하나님, 하늘 위에 높임을 받으십시오. 온 땅 위에 주님의 영광이 [있게 하십시오].
ko.B: 하나님, 하늘보다 높이 높임을 받으십시오. 주님의 영광이 온 땅에 퍼지게 하십시오.
ko.R: 하나님, 주님께서 하늘보다 높으신 분임을 보여 주십시오! 주님의 영광이 온 땅 위에 빛나게 하십시오!

pt.L: Sê exaltado acima dos céus, ó Deus; sobre toda a terra [esteja] a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória.
pt.B: Ó Deus, sê elevado bem acima dos céus; que a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória se espalhe por toda a terra.
pt.R: Ó Deus, mostra que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és mais alto que os céus! Que a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória brilhe sobre a terra inteira!

am.L: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ከሰማያት በላይ ከፍ ከፍ በል፤ ክብርህ በምድር ሁሉ ላይ [ይሁን]።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ከሰማይ በላይ ከፍ ከፍ በል፤ ክብርህ በምድር ሁሉ ላይ ይስፋፋ።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ከሰማይ በላይ እንደ ሆንክ አሳይ! ክብርህ በምድር ሁሉ ላይ ይብራ!

hi.L: हे परमेश्वर, आकाश से ऊपर ऊँचा उठ; सारी पृथ्वी के ऊपर तेरी महिमा [हो]।
hi.B: हे परमेश्वर, आकाश से भी ऊँचा उठ; तेरी महिमा सारी पृथ्वी पर छा जाए।
hi.R: हे परमेश्वर, दिखा दे कि तू आकाश से भी ऊँचा है! तेरी महिमा सारी पृथ्वी पर चमके!

ru.L: Вознесись выше небес, Боже; над всей землёй [да будет] {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава.
ru.B: Боже, будь превознесён выше небес; пусть {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава разольётся по всей земле.
ru.R: Боже, покажи, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} выше небес! Пусть {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава сияет над всей землёй!

ja.L: 天の上に高く上がってください、神よ。全地の上に、あなたの栄光が[あるように]。
ja.B: 神よ、天の上に高く上がってください。あなたの栄光が、全地に広がるように。
ja.R: 神よ、あなたが天よりも高い方であることを示してください！あなたの栄光が、世界中に輝くように！

uk.L: Будь піднесений понад небеса, Боже; над усією землею [нехай буде] {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава.
uk.B: Боже, будь піднесений високо понад небеса; нехай {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава ширяє над усією землею.
uk.R: Боже, покажи, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} вищий за небеса! Нехай {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} слава сяє над усією землею!

decisions.choice: Psalm 57:12
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 57:12 (the refrain of 57:6 and 57:12) word for word, and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: be exalted: show yourself high
decisions.reason: The verb (rum) asks God to show his greatness, so that all the earth sees his glory (57:6).

decisions.choice: show that you are higher than the heavens
decisions.reason: As in 57:6 and 57:12.

decisions.choice: The refrain of 57:6 / 57:12 word for word
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 57:12 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

source.text: לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וַעֲנֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: So that they may be rescued, your beloved ones, save [with] your right hand, and answer me.

en.L: So that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} beloved ones may be rescued, save [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand, and answer me.
en.B: So that those {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love may be set free, bring rescue with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand and answer me!
en.R: Rescue the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love! Save us with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power, and answer my prayer!

fr.L: Afin que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} bien-aimés soient délivrés, sauve [par] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite, et réponds-moi.
fr.B: Pour que ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aimes soient libérés, viens au secours par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main droite et réponds-moi !
fr.R: Délivre le peuple que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aimes ! Sauve-nous par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance, et réponds à ma prière !

sw.L: Ili wapendwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} waokolewe, uokoe [kwa] mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume, unijibu.
sw.B: Ili wale unaowapenda wawekwe huru, lete wokovu kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume, unijibu!
sw.R: Uwaokoe watu unaowapenda! Utuokoe kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kuu, ujibu maombi yangu!

es.L: Para que sean librados {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} amados, salva [con] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} diestra, y respóndeme.
es.B: Para que los que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} amas sean liberados, rescata con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano derecha y respóndeme.
es.R: ¡Rescata a las personas que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} amas! Sálvanos con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder, ¡y responde a mi oración!

vi.L: Để những người yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được giải cứu, xin cứu [bằng] tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đáp lời tôi.
vi.B: Để những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương được giải thoát, xin đưa tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra giải cứu và đáp lời tôi!
vi.R: Xin giải cứu những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương! Xin dùng quyền năng lớn lao của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà cứu chúng con, và xin đáp lời cầu nguyện của tôi!

ko.L: 주님께서 사랑하시는 이들이 건짐을 받도록, 주님의 오른손으로 구원하시고 제게 응답하여 주십시오.
ko.B: 주님께서 사랑하시는 이들이 구출되도록, 주님의 오른손으로 구원을 베푸시고 제게 응답해 주십시오!
ko.R: 주님께서 사랑하시는 사람들을 건져 주십시오! 주님의 큰 능력으로 저희를 구원하시고, 제 기도에 응답해 주십시오!

pt.L: Para que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} amados sejam livrados, salva [com] a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão direita, e responde-me.
pt.B: Para que aqueles que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amas sejam libertados, salva com a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão direita e responde-me!
pt.R: Livra as pessoas que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amas! Salva-nos com o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} grande poder e responde à minha oração!

am.L: ወዳጆችህ ይድኑ ዘንድ፣ በቀኝ እጅህ አድን፤ መልስልኝም።
am.B: የምትወዳቸው ነጻ እንዲወጡ፣ በቀኝ እጅህ ማዳንን አምጣ፤ መልስልኝም!
am.R: የምትወዳቸውን ሰዎች ታደግ! በታላቅ ኃይልህ አድነን፤ ጸሎቴንም መልስ!

hi.L: ताकि तेरे प्रिय छुड़ाए जाएँ, अपने दाहिने हाथ से बचा, और मुझे उत्तर दे।
hi.B: ताकि जिनसे तू प्रेम करता है वे छुटकारा पाएँ, अपने दाहिने हाथ से उद्धार कर और मुझे उत्तर दे!
hi.R: जिनसे तू प्रेम करता है, उन्हें छुड़ा ले! अपनी महान शक्ति से हमें बचा, और मेरी प्रार्थना का उत्तर दे!

ru.L: Чтобы были избавлены {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} возлюбленные, спаси {{deity_pronoun:твоей|Твоей}} правой рукой и ответь мне.
ru.B: Чтобы освободились те, кого {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} любишь, спаси {{deity_pronoun:твоей|Твоей}} правой рукой и ответь мне!
ru.R: Спаси людей, которых {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} любишь! Спаси нас {{deity_pronoun:твоей|Твоей}} великой силой и ответь на мою молитву!

ja.L: あなたの愛する者たちが救い出されるように、あなたの右の手で救い、わたしに答えてください。
ja.B: あなたが愛しておられる者たちが助け出されるように、あなたの右の手で救い、わたしに答えてください！
ja.R: あなたが愛しておられる人たちを、助け出してください！あなたの大きな力で、わたしたちを救い、わたしの祈りに答えてください！

uk.L: Щоб {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} улюблені були визволені, спаси [своєю] правицею й відповідай мені.
uk.B: Щоб ті, кого {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} любиш, були звільнені, принеси порятунок {{deity_pronoun:твоєю|Твоєю}} правицею й відповідай мені!
uk.R: Урятуй людей, яких {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} любиш! Спаси нас {{deity_pronoun:твоєю|Твоєю}} великою силою й відповідай на мою молитву!

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:7
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 repeat 60:7-14 with small differences, and the wording follows it. Here the Hebrew both writes and reads "answer me"; in 60:7 the written form is "answer us".

decisions.choice: right hand: God's power to act
decisions.reason: The right hand is the hand of strength (17:7; 20:7).

decisions.choice: your beloved ones: the people God loves
decisions.reason: The word (yedidim) is used of those dear to God (127:2; Deuteronomy 33:12).

decisions.choice: with your great power
decisions.reason: As in 60:7, Readable says what the right hand stands for (m2).

decisions.choice: us
decisions.reason: As in 60:7, Readable names who is to be saved, the people of the first line.

decisions.choice: "chúng con" (R) for the "us" the English Readable supplies, beside "tôi" for the singer
decisions.reason: When the singer prays to God for the people he says "chúng con", the humble "we" of prayer, as in Psalm 4:7; for himself he keeps "tôi". |

decisions.choice: wording of Psalm 60:7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 are Psalm 60:7-14, and Hindi keeps that psalm's wording at each level, without its line breaks (the English levels here have none); only verses 10 and 12 change, where the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the Russian of Psalm 60:7
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 repeat Psalm 60:7-14 (Hebrew numbering); each level copies that Russian, without the line breaks the English does not have here.

decisions.choice: As 60:7 word for word: yedideikha "あなたの愛する者たち" (L), "あなたが愛しておられる者たち" (B, R); yeminkha "右の手" (L, B), "大きな力" (R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:7 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

source.text: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶעְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: God has spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and [the] Valley of Succoth I will measure off.

en.L: God has spoken in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: "I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and the Valley of Succoth I will measure off.
en.B: God has spoken from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place: "I will rejoice as I share out Shechem and mark off the Valley of Succoth.
en.R: God has spoken from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place. He said, "I have won, and I am glad! I will divide up the land of Shechem and the Valley of Succoth for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

fr.L: Dieu a parlé dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté : « J’exulterai ; je partagerai Sichem, et la vallée de Soukkoth, je [la] mesurerai.
fr.B: Dieu a parlé depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint : « Je me réjouirai en partageant Sichem et en mesurant la vallée de Soukkoth.
fr.R: Dieu a parlé depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint. Il a dit : « J’ai gagné, et je suis heureux ! Je vais partager le pays de Sichem et la vallée de Soukkoth pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple.

sw.L: Mungu amesema katika utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: "Nitashangilia; nitaigawa Shekemu, na Bonde la Sukothi nitalipima.
sw.B: Mungu amesema kutoka mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu: "Nitafurahi nikiigawa Shekemu na kulipima Bonde la Sukothi.
sw.R: Mungu amesema kutoka mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu. Alisema, "Nimeshinda, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nafurahi! Nitaigawa nchi ya Shekemu na Bonde la Sukothi kwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

es.L: Dios ha hablado en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad: «Me regocijaré; repartiré Siquem, y el valle de Sucot mediré.
es.B: Dios ha hablado desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo: «Con alegría repartiré Siquem y mediré el valle de Sucot.
es.R: Dios ha hablado desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo. Dijo: «¡He vencido y estoy contento! Repartiré la tierra de Siquem y el valle de Sucot para {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời đã phán trong sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ta sẽ hân hoan; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chia Si-chem, và thung lũng Su-cốt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đo phần.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời đã phán từ nơi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ta sẽ vui mừng khi chia phần Si-chem và đo đạc thung lũng Su-cốt.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã phán từ nơi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài phán: "Ta đã chiến thắng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vui mừng! Ta sẽ chia đất Si-chem và thung lũng Su-cốt cho dân của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 하나님께서 그분의 거룩하심으로 말씀하셨다. "내가 크게 기뻐하겠다. 내가 세겜을 나누고, 숙곳 골짜기를 측량하겠다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 그분의 거룩한 곳에서 말씀하셨다. "내가 기뻐하며 세겜을 나누어 주고 숙곳 골짜기를 재어 나누겠다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 그분의 거룩한 곳에서 이렇게 말씀하셨다. "내가 이겼으니 기쁘다! 내가 세겜 땅과 숙곳 골짜기를 나누어 내 백성에게 주겠다.

pt.L: Deus falou na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santidade: "Eu exultarei; repartirei Siquém, e o vale de Sucote medirei.
pt.B: Deus falou do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} santo lugar: "Eu me alegrarei ao repartir Siquém e demarcar o vale de Sucote.
pt.R: Deus falou do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} santo lugar. Ele disse: "Eu venci e estou contente! Vou dividir a terra de Siquém e o vale de Sucote para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo.

am.L: እግዚአብሔር በቅድስናው ተናገረ፦ «ደስ ይለኛል፤ ሴኬምን እከፋፍላለሁ፤ የሱኮትንም ሸለቆ እለካለሁ።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ከቅዱስ ስፍራው ተናገረ፦ «ደስ ይለኛል፤ ሴኬምን አካፍላለሁ፤ የሱኮትንም ሸለቆ እሸነሽናለሁ።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ከቅዱስ ስፍራው ተናገረ። እንዲህ አለ፦ «አሸንፌአለሁ፤ ደስም ብሎኛል! የሴኬምን ምድርና የሱኮትን ሸለቆ ለሕዝቤ አከፋፍላለሁ።

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:8
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:8 with the same sense; the wording here follows it.

decisions.choice: in his holiness: from his holy place, or by his holy nature
decisions.reason: As in 60:8: the word (qodesh) can mean holiness or the holy place. God speaks either from his sanctuary or by his holiness, as an oath (89:36).

decisions.choice: Shechem and Succoth: the land given out
decisions.reason: Shechem lay west of the Jordan and Succoth east of it (Genesis 33:17-18). God speaks as a victorious warrior dividing land among his people.

decisions.choice: God's words
decisions.reason: God's speech runs from here to the end of verse 10, as in 60:8-10.

decisions.choice: He said; I have won; for my people
decisions.reason: As in 60:8, Readable makes the start of God's words and the purpose of dividing the land clear.

decisions.choice: God's words quoted with "Ta" for himself, with the deity_pronoun setting in mid-sentence, through verse 10; "Si-chem", "Su-cốt", "Ga-la-át", "Ma-na-se", "Ép-ra-im", "Giu-đa", "Mô-áp", "Ê-đôm", "Phi-li-tin" for the names
decisions.reason: God speaking says "Ta", as in Psalm 2:6. The names take the forms of the Protestant tradition. |

decisions.choice: God's words (verses 8-10) are reported in the plain written style ("하나님께서 ... 말씀하셨다"), and God speaks in 해라체 with "나"
decisions.reason: The verse speaks about God, not to him, so the plain style with the honorific holds; God speaking uses 해라체 with 나 (style guide section 7a).

decisions.choice: As 60:8 word for word; God's speech plain with わたし, opening here and closing in 108:10
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:8 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

en.L: Gilead [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and Manasseh [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; and Ephraim [is] the helmet of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head; Judah [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} scepter.
en.B: Gilead belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Manasseh is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; Ephraim is the helmet on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head, Judah the staff of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rule.
en.R: Gilead and Manasseh belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Ephraim is like a helmet that protects {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head. Judah is the rod I rule with.

fr.R: Galaad et Manassé {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiennent. Éphraïm est comme un casque qui protège {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} tête. Juda est le bâton avec lequel je gouverne.

es.L: Galaad [es] {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, y Manasés [es] {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}; y Efraín [es] el casco de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza; Judá [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cetro.

ko.L: 길르앗이 내 것이요, 므낫세도 내 것이다. 에브라임은 내 머리의 투구요, 유다는 나의 홀이다.
ko.B: 길르앗은 내 것이고 므낫세도 내 것이다. 에브라임은 내 머리에 쓰는 투구요, 유다는 내가 다스리는 지팡이다.
ko.R: 길르앗과 므낫세는 내 것이다. 에브라임은 내 머리를 지키는 투구와 같고, 유다는 내가 다스릴 때 쓰는 지팡이다.

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:9
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:9 with the same sense; the wording here follows it.

decisions.choice: Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah: Israel's own tribes
decisions.reason: As in 60:9: Gilead lay east of the Jordan, Manasseh lived on both sides of it, Ephraim was the strongest tribe in the north and Judah the royal tribe in the south. God claims them all as his own.

decisions.choice: my scepter: the staff of the ruler
decisions.reason: As in 60:9, the word (mechoqeq) recalls Jacob's blessing of Judah (Genesis 49:10).

decisions.choice: the protection of my head: a helmet
decisions.reason: The phrase means a stronghold for the head, that is, a helmet.

decisions.choice: As 60:9 word for word: "ギレアド", "マナセ", "エフライム", "ユダ"; mechoqeqi "王笏" (L), "支配の杖" (B), "国を治めるつえ" (R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:9 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

en.B: Moab is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} washing bowl; on Edom I toss {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sandal; I raise the victor's shout over Philistia!"
en.R: Moab is only a bowl I wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet in. I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sandal on Edom to show it is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. I shout in triumph over Philistia!"

sw.L: Moabu [ni] bakuli {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la kunawia; juu ya Edomu natupa kiatu {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}; juu ya Ufilisti napiga kelele za ushindi."

es.L: Moab [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lavatorio; sobre Edom echo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sandalia; sobre Filistea grito en triunfo».

es.R: Moab no es más que una palangana donde lavo {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} pies. Arrojaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sandalia sobre Edom para mostrar que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. ¡Grito en triunfo sobre Filistea!».

vi.L: Mô-áp [là] chậu rửa của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; trên Ê-đôm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ném chiếc dép của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; trên Phi-li-tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} reo hò chiến thắng."

vi.R: Mô-áp chỉ là cái chậu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} dùng để rửa chân. Ta sẽ ném chiếc dép của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lên Ê-đôm để tỏ ra đất ấy thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta reo hò chiến thắng trên Phi-li-tin!"

ko.L: 모압은 내 씻는 대야요, 에돔 위에 내가 내 신을 던지고, 블레셋 위에서 내가 승리의 함성을 지른다."
ko.B: 모압은 내 발 씻는 대야이다. 에돔 위에 내가 신을 던지고, 블레셋을 두고 승리의 함성을 지르겠다!"

pt.L: Moabe [é] a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} bacia de lavar; sobre Edom lanço a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} sandália; sobre a Filístia grito em triunfo."
pt.B: Moabe é a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} bacia de lavar; sobre Edom atiro a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} sandália; sobre a Filístia levanto o grito de vitória!"
pt.R: Moabe é só uma bacia onde eu lavo os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} pés. Vou atirar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} sandália sobre Edom para mostrar que ele é {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}}. Sobre a Filístia eu grito em triunfo!"

am.L: ሞዓብ የመታጠቢያ ሳሕኔ ነው፤ በኤዶም ላይ ጫማዬን እወረውራለሁ፤ በፍልስጥኤም ላይ በድል እልል እላለሁ።»
am.B: ሞዓብ የመታጠቢያ ሳሕኔ ነው፤ በኤዶም ላይ ጫማዬን እጥላለሁ፤ በፍልስጥኤም ላይ የአሸናፊ እልልታ አሰማለሁ!»
am.R: ሞዓብ እግሬን የምታጠብበት ሳሕን ብቻ ነው። የእኔ መሆኑን ለማሳየት ጫማዬን በኤዶም ላይ እጥላለሁ። በፍልስጥኤም ላይ በድል እልል እላለሁ!»

hi.L: मोआब मेरे धोने का पात्र [है]; एदोम पर मैं अपनी जूती फेंकूँगा; पलिश्त पर मैं जयजयकार करूँगा।"
hi.B: मोआब मेरे हाथ-पैर धोने का पात्र है; एदोम पर मैं अपनी जूती उछालूँगा; पलिश्त पर मैं विजय का नारा लगाऊँगा!"
hi.R: मोआब बस एक बर्तन है जिसमें मैं अपने पैर धोता हूँ। मैं एदोम पर अपनी जूती फेंकूँगा, यह दिखाने के लिए कि वह मेरा है। मैं पलिश्त पर जीत की जयजयकार करता हूँ!"

ru.L: Моав — {{deity_pronoun:моя|Моя}} умывальная чаша; на Едом брошу {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} сандалию; над Филистией {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} издам победный клич.»
ru.B: Моав — {{deity_pronoun:моя|Моя}} чаша для умывания; на Едом {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} брошу {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} сандалию; над Филистией {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} издам клич победителя!»
ru.R: Моав — всего лишь таз, в котором {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} мою ноги. Я брошу {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} сандалию на Едом, чтобы показать, что он {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}}. Я с победным кличем торжествую над Филистией!»

ja.L: モアブは、わたしの洗い鉢。エドムの上に、わたしは履物を投げる。ペリシテの上に、わたしは勝ちどきをあげる。」
ja.B: モアブは、わたしが足を洗うたらい。エドムの上に、わたしは履物を投げる。ペリシテに向かって、わたしは勝利の叫びをあげる！」
ja.R: モアブは、わたしが足を洗うたらいにすぎない。わたしは、エドムの上に履物を投げて、そこがわたしのものであることを示す。わたしはペリシテに勝って、勝利の叫びをあげる！」

uk.L: Моав — {{deity_pronoun:моя|Моя}} умивальниця; на Едом я кину {{deity_pronoun:мій|Мій}} сандаль; над Филистеєю я вигукую з тріумфом.»
uk.B: Моав — {{deity_pronoun:моя|Моя}} миска для вмивання; на Едом я кидаю {{deity_pronoun:мій|Мій}} сандаль; над Филистеєю я здіймаю переможний вигук!»
uk.R: Моав — лише миска, у якій я мию {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} ноги. Я кину {{deity_pronoun:мій|Мій}} сандаль на Едом, щоб показати, що він — {{deity_pronoun:мій|Мій}}. Я з тріумфом вигукую над Филистеєю!»

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:10
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:10, except the last line: 60:10 has "over me, Philistia, shout aloud", where this verse has "over Philistia I shout in triumph". The first two lines follow 60:10.

decisions.choice: my washbasin: the lowest servant's task
decisions.reason: As in 60:10, Moab will be like a basin for washing the feet: the proud neighbor becomes God's servant.

decisions.choice: throw my sandal: claim as one's own
decisions.reason: Throwing or setting down a sandal on land was a way of claiming it (Ruth 4:7).

decisions.choice: shout in triumph: the victor's shout
decisions.reason: The verb (rua', reflexive) is the shout of a winner over a beaten enemy. Here God himself shouts over Philistia.

decisions.choice: to show it is mine
decisions.reason: As in 60:10, Readable explains the picture (m3).

decisions.choice: sobre a Filístia grito em triunfo (L) / levanto o grito de vitória (B, R)
decisions.reason: The first two lines keep the words of 60:10; the last line differs in the Hebrew (m1): here God himself raises the victor's shout over Philistia (m4), so the Portuguese no longer addresses Philistia as 60:10 does.

decisions.choice: last line "በፍልስጥኤም ላይ በድል እልል እላለሁ" (L, R), "የአሸናፊ እልልታ አሰማለሁ" (B): God shouts over Philistia
decisions.reason: 60:10 has "over me, Philistia, shout aloud" (ፍልስጥኤም ሆይ ... እልል በዪ); this verse has "over Philistia I shout in triumph". The first two lines keep the Amharic of 60:10.

decisions.choice: पलिश्त पर मैं जयजयकार करूँगा
alternatives: हे पलिश्त, मेरे कारण जयजयकार करो
decisions.reason: Psalm 60:10 reads "over me, Philistia, shout aloud"; here the Hebrew has "over Philistia I shout in triumph", so the last line changes to God's own victory shout while the first two lines keep 60:10's wording.

decisions.choice: над Филистией я издам победный клич
decisions.reason: Psalm 60:10 has Philistia shout over God; here God shouts in triumph over Philistia, so the last line is new and the rest keeps the Russian of 60:10.

decisions.choice: 'alei-Feleshet 'etro'a' "ペリシテの上に、わたしは勝ちどきをあげる" (L), "ペリシテに向かって、わたしは勝利の叫びをあげる" (B, R), where 60:10 has God's command "ペリシテよ、…叫びなさい"
decisions.reason: 108:10 has God himself shouting in triumph over Philistia (m4), where 60:10 tells Philistia to shout; the first two lines are 60:10's Japanese. The speech of God closes here, as in the English.

source.text: מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מִבְצָ֑ר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will bring me [to the] city of fortification? Who has led me to Edom?

en.L: Who will bring me [to the] fortified city? Who has led me to Edom?
en.B: Who will take me into the walled city? Who will guide me all the way to Edom?
en.R: Who will lead me into the strong city of Edom? Who will take me there?

fr.L: Qui me conduira [à la] ville fortifiée ? Qui m’a mené jusqu’à Édom ?
fr.B: Qui me fera entrer dans la ville aux remparts ? Qui me guidera jusqu’en Édom ?
fr.R: Qui me fera entrer dans la ville forte d’Édom ? Qui m’y conduira ?

sw.L: Ni nani atakayenileta [mpaka] mji wenye ngome? Ni nani aliyeniongoza mpaka Edomu?
sw.B: Ni nani atakayenipeleka ndani ya mji wenye kuta? Ni nani atakayeniongoza mpaka Edomu?
sw.R: Ni nani atakayeniongoza kuingia katika mji imara wa Edomu? Ni nani atakayenipeleka huko?

es.L: ¿Quién me llevará [a la] ciudad fortificada? ¿Quién me ha guiado hasta Edom?
es.B: ¿Quién me hará entrar en la ciudad amurallada? ¿Quién me guiará hasta Edom?
es.R: ¿Quién me llevará a la ciudad fuerte de Edom? ¿Quién me llevará allí?

vi.L: Ai sẽ đưa tôi vào thành kiên cố? Ai đã dẫn tôi đến Ê-đôm?
vi.B: Ai sẽ đưa tôi vào thành có tường vững chắc? Ai sẽ dẫn tôi đến tận Ê-đôm?
vi.R: Ai sẽ dẫn tôi vào thành vững chắc của Ê-đôm? Ai sẽ đưa tôi đến đó?

ko.L: 누가 나를 요새의 성으로 데려가겠는가? 누가 나를 에돔까지 인도하였는가?
ko.B: 누가 나를 성벽 두른 성으로 데려가겠는가? 누가 나를 에돔까지 이끌어 주겠는가?
ko.R: 누가 나를 에돔의 튼튼한 성으로 이끌어 들이겠는가? 누가 나를 그곳에 데려가겠는가?

pt.L: Quem me levará [à] cidade fortificada? Quem me conduziu até Edom?
pt.B: Quem me fará entrar na cidade cercada de muralhas? Quem me guiará até Edom?
pt.R: Quem vai me levar para dentro da cidade forte de Edom? Quem vai me levar até lá?

am.L: ወደ ተመሸገችው ከተማ ማን ያመጣኛል? እስከ ኤዶምስ ማን መራኝ?
am.B: ወደ ቅጥሯ ከተማ ማን ያስገባኛል? እስከ ኤዶም ድረስ ማን ይመራኛል?
am.R: ወደ ኤዶም ጠንካራ ከተማ ማን ይመራኛል? ወደዚያስ ማን ይወስደኛል?

hi.L: कौन मुझे गढ़वाले नगर [में] पहुँचाएगा? कौन मुझे एदोम तक ले गया है?
hi.B: कौन मुझे उस शहरपनाहवाले नगर में ले जाएगा? कौन मुझे एदोम तक पहुँचाएगा?
hi.R: कौन मुझे एदोम के मज़बूत नगर में ले जाएगा? कौन मुझे वहाँ पहुँचाएगा?

ru.L: Кто введёт меня в укреплённый город? Кто привёл меня в Едом?
ru.B: Кто введёт меня в город за стенами? Кто доведёт меня до самого Едома?
ru.R: Кто поведёт меня в крепкий город Едома? Кто приведёт меня туда?

ja.L: だれが、わたしを堅固な町に連れて行くだろうか？だれが、わたしをエドムまで導いてくれたか？
ja.B: だれが、わたしを城壁のある町に連れて行くだろうか？だれが、わたしをエドムまで導いてくれるだろうか？
ja.R: だれが、わたしをエドムの強い町に連れて行ってくれるだろうか？だれが、わたしをそこへ連れて行ってくれるだろうか？

uk.L: Хто приведе мене [до] укріпленого міста? Хто повів мене до Едому?
uk.B: Хто введе мене в обнесене мурами місто? Хто проведе мене аж до Едому?
uk.R: Хто поведе мене в міцне місто Едому? Хто приведе мене туди?

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:11
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:11. 60:11 uses another word for "fortified" (matsor) where this verse has mivtsar; the sense is the same, and the wording follows 60:11.

decisions.choice: the fortified city: Edom's stronghold
decisions.reason: Probably Bozrah or Sela, the rock city of Edom (2 Kings 14:7), hard to take by force.

decisions.choice: has led me: who could lead me
decisions.reason: As in 60:11, the verb is past in form; the question is the same as the first. After God's words, the speaker is the king or the people.

decisions.choice: The king's questions are in the plain style with "나"; verses 12-13 turn to God in 합쇼체 with "저희"
decisions.reason: The questions are asked aloud, not yet to God; the answer, addressed to God, comes in verse 12 ("is it not you, God?"), and Korean marks that turn by the speech level.

decisions.choice: As 60:11 word for word: 'ir mivtsar "堅固な町" (L), "城壁のある町" (B), "エドムの強い町" (R); nachani "導いてくれたか" (L), "導いてくれるだろうか" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:11 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not God [who] has rejected us? And not you go out, God, with our armies.

en.L: [Is it] not [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], God, [who] have rejected us? And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go out, God, with our armies.
en.B: Is it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, who rejected us and no longer march out with our armies?
en.R: God, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can lead us, even though {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from us. You no longer go with our armies into battle.

fr.L: N’[est-ce] pas [{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}], ô Dieu, [qui] nous as rejetés ? Et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sors pas, ô Dieu, avec nos armées.
fr.B: N’est-ce pas {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, ô Dieu, qui nous as rejetés et qui ne sors plus avec nos armées ?
fr.R: Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} seul peux nous conduire, même si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}es détourné de nous. Tu ne vas plus avec nos armées à la bataille.

sw.L: Je, si [{{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}], Ee Mungu, uliyetukataa? Wala hutoki, Ee Mungu, pamoja na majeshi yetu.
sw.B: Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee Mungu, uliyetukataa, na hutoki tena pamoja na majeshi yetu?
sw.R: Ee Mungu, ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} tu unayeweza kutuongoza, ingawa umetuacha. Hutoki tena pamoja na majeshi yetu kwenda vitani.

es.L: ¿No [eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}], oh Dios, [quien] nos ha rechazado? Y no sales, oh Dios, con nuestros ejércitos.
es.B: ¿No eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, oh Dios, quien nos rechazó y ya no sale con nuestros ejércitos?
es.R: Dios, solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes guiarnos, aunque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos has dado la espalda. Ya no vas con nuestros ejércitos a la batalla.

vi.L: Há chẳng phải [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], lạy Đức Chúa Trời, [là Đấng] đã từ bỏ chúng con sao? Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không ra đi, lạy Đức Chúa Trời, với quân đội chúng con.
vi.B: Há chẳng phải chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy Đức Chúa Trời, là Đấng đã từ bỏ chúng con và không còn ra trận cùng quân đội chúng con sao?
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, chỉ có {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mới có thể dẫn dắt chúng con, dù {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quay lưng lại với chúng con. Ngài không còn đi cùng quân đội chúng con ra trận nữa.

ko.L: 하나님, 저희를 버리신 [분은 주님이] 아니십니까? 하나님, 주님께서는 저희 군대와 함께 나가지 않으십니다.
ko.B: 하나님, 저희를 버리시고 더는 저희 군대와 함께 나가지 않으시는 분이 바로 주님이 아니십니까?
ko.R: 하나님, 주님께서 저희에게서 돌아서셨지만, 저희를 이끄실 수 있는 분은 주님뿐입니다. 주님께서는 이제 저희 군대와 함께 싸움터에 나가지 않으십니다.

pt.L: Não [foste {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}], ó Deus, [que] nos rejeitaste? E {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não sais, ó Deus, com os nossos exércitos.
pt.B: Não foste {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, ó Deus, que nos rejeitaste e já não sais com os nossos exércitos?
pt.R: Ó Deus, só {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes nos guiar, mesmo que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nos tenhas deixado de lado. Tu já não vais com os nossos exércitos para a batalha.

am.L: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ የጣልኸን [አንተ] አይደለህምን? እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ከሠራዊታችንም ጋር አትወጣም።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ የጣልኸን ከሠራዊታችንም ጋር ከእንግዲህ የማትወጣ አንተ አይደለህምን?
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ ከእኛ ዘወር ብትልም እንኳ ሊመራን የሚችል አንተ ብቻ ነህ። አሁን ግን ከሠራዊታችን ጋር ወደ ጦርነት አትሄድም።

hi.L: हे परमेश्वर, क्या [तूने ही] हमें नहीं त्यागा? और हे परमेश्वर, तू हमारी सेनाओं के साथ नहीं निकलता।
hi.B: हे परमेश्वर, क्या तू ही नहीं है जिसने हमें ठुकरा दिया और अब हमारी सेनाओं के साथ नहीं निकलता?
hi.R: हे परमेश्वर, केवल तू ही हमारी अगुवाई कर सकता है, चाहे तूने हमसे मुँह फेर लिया हो। तू अब युद्ध में हमारी सेनाओं के साथ नहीं जाता।

ru.L: Не [{{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}}] ли, Боже, отверг нас? И {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} не выходишь, Боже, с нашими войсками.
ru.B: Не {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} ли, Боже, отверг нас и больше не выходишь с нашими войсками?
ru.R: Боже, только {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} можешь вести нас, хотя {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} и отвернулся от нас. Ты больше не ходишь с нашими войсками в бой.

ja.L: 神よ、わたしたちを退けられたのは、[あなた]ではないか？神よ、あなたは、わたしたちの軍勢と共に出て行くことはなさらない。
ja.B: 神よ、あなたは、わたしたちを退け、もはや、わたしたちの軍勢と共に出て行くことをなさらないのではないか？
ja.R: 神よ、わたしたちを導くことができるのは、あなただけだ。あなたが、わたしたちから離れてしまわれたとしても。あなたは、もう、わたしたちの軍隊と一緒に戦いに出てくださらない。

uk.L: Хіба не [{{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}}], Боже, [що] відкинув нас? І {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} не виходиш, Боже, з нашими військами.
uk.B: Хіба не {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}}, Боже, відкинув нас і більше не виступаєш із нашими військами?
uk.R: Боже, лише {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} можеш вести нас, хоч {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} відвернувся від нас. Ти більше не йдеш із нашими військами в бій.

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:12
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:12, which adds the pronoun "you" ("is it not you, God"). The sense is the same, and the wording follows 60:12; Literal brackets "you" here.

decisions.choice: Is it not you? the answer to verse 11
decisions.reason: As in 60:12: the only one who can lead the king to Edom is God, the very God who has seemed to reject his people.

decisions.choice: go out with our armies: lead them in battle
decisions.reason: God went out before Israel's armies (Judges 4:14). His absence meant defeat (44:10).

decisions.choice: only you can lead us
decisions.reason: As in 60:12, Readable spells out the answer the question implies (m2).

decisions.choice: leaving out the second "God"
decisions.reason: As in 60:12, Balanced gives the address once; Literal keeps both.

decisions.choice: Literal brackets "[አንተ]"
decisions.reason: 60:12 has the pronoun "you"; 108:12 lacks it, so Literal brackets it, as the English Literal does. Balanced and Readable keep the Amharic of 60:12.
Psalm 60:12 has the pronoun "you"; here the Hebrew lacks it, so Literal brackets it, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: [ты]
decisions.reason: Psalm 60:12 has "you" in the Hebrew; here it does not, so Literal brackets it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: As 60:12, with L "[あなた]" in brackets: 108:12 has no 'attah; God's negative "出て行くことはなさらない" (L, B), "出てくださらない" (R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); 60:12's Japanese is copied without its line breaks. 108:12 lacks 60:12's 'you', so L brackets it as the English L does.

source.text: הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Give to us help from [the] foe, and worthless [is the] salvation of humankind.

en.L: Give us help against [the] foe, for worthless [is] the salvation of humankind.
en.B: Help us against the enemy, for any rescue that people can bring is useless.
en.R: Help us fight the enemy. No human being can save us.

fr.L: Donne-nous du secours contre [l’]adversaire, car vain [est] le salut [qui vient] de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.B: Aide-nous contre l’ennemi, car le secours que les humains peuvent apporter ne sert à rien.
fr.R: Aide-nous à combattre l’ennemi. Aucun être humain ne peut nous sauver.

sw.L: Utupe msaada dhidi ya mtesi, kwa maana wokovu wa mwanadamu [ni] bure.
sw.B: Utusaidie dhidi ya adui, kwa maana msaada wowote ambao watu wanaweza kuleta hauna faida.
sw.R: Utusaidie kupigana na adui. Hakuna mwanadamu anayeweza kutuokoa.

es.L: Danos ayuda contra [el] adversario, porque vana [es] la salvación del ser humano.
es.B: Ayúdanos contra el enemigo, porque cualquier rescate que pueda dar la gente no sirve de nada.
es.R: Ayúdanos a luchar contra el enemigo. Ningún ser humano nos puede salvar.

vi.L: Xin ban cho chúng con sự giúp đỡ chống lại kẻ thù, vì vô ích [là] sự giải cứu của loài người.
vi.B: Xin giúp chúng con chống lại kẻ thù, vì mọi sự giải cứu loài người đem lại đều vô ích.
vi.R: Xin giúp chúng con chiến đấu với kẻ thù. Không một con người nào có thể cứu chúng con.

ko.L: 대적에 맞서 저희에게 도움을 주십시오. 사람의 구원은 헛되기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 원수를 막아 내도록 저희를 도와주십시오. 사람이 베푸는 구원은 아무 소용이 없습니다.
ko.R: 저희가 원수와 싸우도록 도와주십시오. 사람은 아무도 저희를 구할 수 없습니다.

pt.L: Dá-nos ajuda contra [o] adversário, porque vã [é] a salvação da humanidade.
pt.B: Ajuda-nos contra o inimigo, pois qualquer socorro que venha das pessoas é inútil.
pt.R: Ajuda-nos a lutar contra o inimigo. Nenhum ser humano pode nos salvar.

am.L: በባላጋራ ላይ እርዳታን ስጠን፤ የሰው ማዳን ከንቱ ነውና።
am.B: በጠላት ላይ እርዳን፤ ሰዎች የሚያመጡት ማዳን ሁሉ ከንቱ ነውና።
am.R: ጠላትን እንድንዋጋ እርዳን። ሊያድነን የሚችል ሰው የለም።

hi.L: शत्रु के विरुद्ध हमें सहायता दे, क्योंकि मनुष्य का उद्धार व्यर्थ [है]।
hi.B: शत्रु के विरुद्ध हमारी सहायता कर, क्योंकि मनुष्य जो छुटकारा दे सकते हैं, वह बेकार है।
hi.R: शत्रु से लड़ने में हमारी सहायता कर। कोई मनुष्य हमें नहीं बचा सकता।

ru.L: Дай нам помощь против врага, ведь тщетно спасение человеческое.
ru.B: Помоги нам против врага, ведь всякое спасение от людей бесполезно.
ru.R: Помоги нам сражаться с врагом. Ни один человек не может спасти нас.

ja.L: 仇に対する助けを、わたしたちに与えてください。人の救いは、むなしいからだ。
ja.B: 仇に立ち向かうわたしたちを、助けてください。人がもたらす救いは、何の役にも立たないからだ。
ja.R: 敵と戦うわたしたちを、助けてください。人間には、わたしたちを救うことはできない。

uk.L: Дай нам допомогу проти супротивника, бо марне — спасіння від людини.
uk.B: Допоможи нам проти ворога, бо будь-який порятунок, що можуть дати люди, — марний.
uk.R: Допоможи нам битися з ворогом. Жодна людина не може нас спасти.

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:13
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:13 with the same sense; the wording here follows it.

decisions.choice: worthless: empty, in vain
decisions.reason: The word (shav') means emptiness; human help cannot save (33:16-17; 146:3).

decisions.choice: and: for
decisions.reason: The "and" gives the reason for the plea.

decisions.choice: As 60:13 word for word: tsar "仇" (L, B), "敵" (R); teshu'at 'adam "人の救い" (L), "人がもたらす救い" (B)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:13 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.

records.literal_gloss: In God we will do strength, and he will tread down our foes.

en.L: In God we will do valiantly, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will tread down our foes.
en.B: With God on our side we will fight with courage; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who will crush our foes underfoot.
en.R: With God's help we will fight bravely. He will trample our enemies.

fr.L: En Dieu nous ferons des exploits, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} écrasera nos adversaires.
fr.B: Avec Dieu à nos côtés, nous combattrons avec courage ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui piétinera nos ennemis.
fr.R: Avec l’aide de Dieu, nous combattrons avec courage. Il écrasera nos ennemis.

sw.L: Katika Mungu tutatenda kwa ushujaa, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawakanyaga watesi wetu.
sw.B: Mungu akiwa upande wetu tutapigana kwa ujasiri; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye atakayewaponda adui zetu chini ya miguu.
sw.R: Kwa msaada wa Mungu tutapigana kwa ushujaa. Yeye atawakanyaga adui zetu.

es.L: Con Dios haremos proezas, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pisoteará a nuestros adversarios.
es.B: Con Dios de nuestro lado lucharemos con valor; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es quien pisoteará a nuestros enemigos.
es.R: Con la ayuda de Dios lucharemos con valentía. Él pisoteará a nuestros enemigos.

vi.L: Nhờ Đức Chúa Trời, chúng ta sẽ làm việc dũng mãnh, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ giày đạp kẻ thù chúng ta.
vi.B: Có Đức Chúa Trời ở cùng, chúng ta sẽ chiến đấu can đảm; chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ chà đạp kẻ thù chúng ta dưới chân.
vi.R: Nhờ Đức Chúa Trời giúp đỡ, chúng ta sẽ chiến đấu dũng cảm. Ngài sẽ giày đạp kẻ thù của chúng ta.

ko.L: 하나님 안에서 우리가 용맹을 떨칠 것이니, 바로 그분께서 우리의 대적들을 짓밟으실 것이다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 우리 편이시니 우리는 용감하게 싸울 것이다. 우리의 원수들을 발아래 짓밟으실 분은 바로 그분이시다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 도와주시니 우리는 용감하게 싸울 것이다. 그분께서 우리의 원수들을 짓밟으실 것이다.

pt.L: Em Deus agiremos com valentia, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pisará os nossos adversários.
pt.B: Com Deus do nosso lado lutaremos com coragem; é {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quem vai esmagar debaixo dos pés os nossos adversários.
pt.R: Com a ajuda de Deus vamos lutar com bravura. Ele vai pisar os nossos inimigos.

am.L: በእግዚአብሔር ጀግንነትን እናደርጋለን፤ እርሱም ባላጋራዎቻችንን ይረግጣል።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ከጎናችን ሆኖ በብርታት እንዋጋለን፤ ጠላቶቻችንን ከእግሩ በታች የሚጨፈልቃቸው እርሱ ነው።
am.R: በእግዚአብሔር እርዳታ በጀግንነት እንዋጋለን። እርሱ ጠላቶቻችንን ይረግጣል።

hi.L: परमेश्वर में हम वीरता करेंगे, और वे हमारे शत्रुओं को रौंद डालेंगे।
hi.B: परमेश्वर हमारे साथ हों तो हम साहस से लड़ेंगे; वही हैं जो हमारे बैरियों को पैरों तले कुचल डालेंगे।
hi.R: परमेश्वर की सहायता से हम वीरता से लड़ेंगे। वे हमारे शत्रुओं को रौंद डालेंगे।

ru.L: С Богом мы явим силу, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} растопчет наших врагов.
ru.B: С Богом на нашей стороне мы будем сражаться отважно; {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} — тот, кто растопчет наших врагов.
ru.R: С Божьей помощью мы будем сражаться храбро. Он растопчет наших врагов.

ja.L: 神にあって、わたしたちは力ある働きをする。その方が、わたしたちの仇を踏みにじられる。
ja.B: 神が共におられるので、わたしたちは勇敢に戦う。わたしたちの仇を踏みつぶしてくださるのは、その方だ。
ja.R: 神の助けによって、わたしたちは勇ましく戦う。神が、わたしたちの敵を踏みつけてくださる。

uk.L: З Богом ми чинитимемо звитяжно, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} потопче наших супротивників.
uk.B: З Богом на нашому боці ми битимемося відважно; {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} — той, хто розтопче наших ворогів.
uk.R: З Божою допомогою ми битимемося хоробро. Він потопче наших ворогів.

decisions.choice: Psalm 60:14
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 60:14 word for word, and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: do strength: act with courage and win
decisions.reason: The phrase means to act bravely and with success (118:15-16; Numbers 24:18).

decisions.choice: he: God himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: God, not the army, will win the victory.

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" (we, including the hearers) when the singer speaks about God to the people, after "chúng con" in the prayer of verses 12-13
decisions.reason: Verse 14 speaks of God as "he", no longer to him; Vietnamese marks the turn by moving from the "chúng con" of prayer to the inclusive "chúng ta".

decisions.choice: The last verse speaks about God in the plain style, with "우리" (we)
alternatives: 저희 and 합쇼체 as in verses 12-13
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from "you" to "he", a word of confidence spoken about God; Korean follows the turn with the plain style and "우리", as style guide section 7a sets for speech about God.

decisions.choice: As 60:14 word for word: na'aseh chayil "力ある働きをする" (L), "勇敢に戦う" (B), "勇ましく戦う" (R); vehu "その方が" (L, B), "神が" (R)
decisions.reason: Psalm 108 is made of 57:8-12 and 60:7-14 (m1); where the Hebrew is the same, the Japanese of 60:14 is copied word for word at each level, without its line breaks, since the English of Psalm 108 has none.
